subject: Residency runbook request: aligning retention & deletion for ACME marketplace listing
messages:
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Residency runbook request for marketplace listing

Hi Vivek,

We're getting close to the ACME listing going live in the Redwood Marketplace. Before we publish we need a short runbook that explains how Redwood will map data residency, retention, and deletion rules across AWS/GCP/Azure — specifically:

- Which cloud region(s) will host customer data for US-based buyers vs EU buyers?
- Retention categories (customer content, logs/telemetry, backups/snapshots) and default retention periods.
- What triggers and timelines exist for complete data deletion (including snapshots and cached content)?
- Any cross-region backup or disaster-recovery practices that could cause data replication outside the requested jurisdiction.

Our legal & procurement teams want this documented so we can attach it to the SOW and include a clause in the marketplace listing. Can you share that runbook or a short Q&A by EOD Wed?

Thanks,
Jordan Hayes
Senior Cloud Security, ACME Corp
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 12:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency runbook request for marketplace listing

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the list of asks. Quick confirmation: is ACME planning to restrict buyer geography at the listing level (i.e., only US buyers) or will buyers in EU be able to purchase the same listing? That affects region mapping and backup placement.

I’ve looped in Marissa (partner manager) and Neha (security/compliance) to draft the runbook. To focus the document, can you confirm two things:

1) Target retention defaults you expect for each classification (if you have specific numbers): customer content, analytics/telemetry, backups/snapshots, and audit logs.
2) Whether ACME requires region-locking (no cross-region backups) or allows disaster recovery replicas in a nearby region within the same cloud provider.

We can deliver a short Q&A + an attachment with a region-by-cloud mapping and deletion playbook. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min sync Wed afternoon.

-Signed,
Vivek Kulkarni
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency runbook request for marketplace listing

Jordan — putting a short draft matrix in the attached spreadsheet (residency-diff-matrix.xlsx). TL;DR draft proposals we plan to include in the public runbook:

- Region mapping (default behavior):
  * US buyers: primary compute & object storage pinned to AWS us-east-1; replicas (if allowed) limited to us-west-2.
  * EU buyers: primary compute & object storage pinned to GCP europe-west1.
  * APAC buyers: (if enabled) Azure eastus2 or partner-hosted APAC region — we can opt-in per listing.

- Retention defaults (configurable per-customer):
  * Customer content (generated prompts + outputs): default 90 days, configurable 30–730 days.
  * Application logs/telemetry: default 365 days; aggregate metrics retained 730 days.
  * Backups & snapshots: default 90 days; snapshot deletion policy runs 7 days after retention expiry to allow restore window.
  * Audit logs (security/auth): default 730 days (for enterprise customers we can extend).

- Deletion & propagation:
  * Deletion request from a buyer triggers: removal of active objects, queuing of snapshot deletion job, TTL-based purge of caches (CDN/in-memory) and a background job to scrub metadata indexes.
  * Snapshot & backup deletion is batched to avoid accidental corruption; full purge completes within 7–21 days depending on workload and legal holds.
  * Cross-region replication: by default disabled for region-locked listings; enabled only if customer opts in for DR and signs off on cross-region replication clause.

- Compliance notes:
  * SOC 2 controls apply across hosted & dedicated offerings.
  * For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, we provide a separate runbook and can support on-prem pinning.

Attached: residency-diff-matrix.xlsx (region mappings + sample SLA language). I also added a draft clause for the listing and a DocuSign link for the SLA if you want to push it to procurement.

Proposed times for a 30-min call: Wed 14:00–16:00 PT or Thu 09:00–11:00 PT. Tell us what works.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procure@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency runbook request for marketplace listing

Thanks Marissa — the matrix looks close to what we need. Two quick clarifications before we lock this in:

1) CDN / edge cache invalidation: when customer content is deleted, how quickly do you invalidate CDN edges and purge cached responses that may contain PII? We need a documented SLA window for cache purge.
2) Snapshot lifecycle: you mention 7–21 days to full purge after deletion — is there an option to expedite to <72 hours for customers that purchase an elevated compliance add-on?

Procurement is happy with the DocuSign flow; I’ve CC’d them. We’re available Wed 14:30 PT if that time is still open.
